title: Using a sledgehammer to crack a nut? Lexical diversity and event coreference resolution
research_question: Is EventCorefBank representative of the lexical and event diversity found in large news streams, and can its coverage be improved by adding distinct instances of the same event types?
methodology: The authors assess the representativeness of EventCorefBank with respect to the broader population of high-volume news. They find that its domains usually center on a single seminal event and therefore augment it with 502 additional texts describing different instances of event types already present in its 43 topics. The augmented resource is released as ECB+ for subsequent event-coreference research.

key_findings.finding: EventCorefBank generally covers only one seminal event within a domain, substantially simplifying the diversity encountered in real news streams.
Introducing different instances of already represented event types increases the corpus's lexical and event diversity.
The augmentation adds 502 texts spanning alternative instances associated with the 43 existing ECB topics.
The resulting ECB+ corpus is intended to provide a more representative resource for event-coreference research on web news.

limitations: Only the abstract was accessible, so detailed experimental procedures and quantitative analyses could not be verified.
The corpus remains focused on news rather than workplace communication.
The augmentation is organized around the 43 event-topic domains already represented in ECB rather than unrestricted open-domain communication.
The accessible abstract does not report downstream coreference-system performance on the augmented corpus.
raw_claims: EventCorefBank is used as an evaluation resource for event coreference.
Its original topic domains usually concentrate on one seminal event.
That structure understates the event and lexical diversity of broader news streams.
The authors add 502 texts describing alternative instances of existing event types.
The expansion covers event types associated with the 43 existing ECB topics.
The augmented resource is released as ECB+ for further research.
